Subject: WarehouseWorks on-prem K8s intake: edge sites & IoT inference requirements

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking this call earlier — following up with our high-level intake so your team can size the cluster and surface any blocker(s) for us. We're WarehouseWorks (logistics IoT), planning a private Kubernetes deployment at four regional warehouses. Key constraints and asks: 

- Each site will host ~12 inference devices that stream preprocessed sensor data to a local K8s pool for real-time predictions; occasional batch sync to central object store.
- Hot inference requires local NVMe-backed node pool for low-latency (<20ms) per-request. Cold storage tier is an on-prem S3-compatible appliance with eventual replication to our central bucket.
- Network: sites use a managed MPLS / customer VPN to the central DC; some sites have restricted outbound egress and strict firewall rules.
- Security/compliance: all PVs must be encrypted at rest; KV cache must not leak secrets to hosts. We're prepping the security questionnaire (attached).

Attached is a simple site inventory CSV. We'd like an operations readout: recommended cluster footprint per site (control plane options), node pool layout (cpu/gpu/ssd), PV class guidance, and any network gating that would block rollout. Also please call out anything that would force us to choose Hosted vs Private deployment.

Can you propose a short mutual action plan and tentative dates? We're aiming for a pilot at one warehouse in Q3.

Thanks,
David Porter
Infrastructure PM, WarehouseWorks
Attachments: site-inventory.csv

Team — forwarding WarehouseWorks' intake. Quick notes / asks from infra ops perspective before we scope SOW: 

1) Control plane model options:
   - Option A (recommended for pilot): single-site managed control plane (HA pair) hosted in customer DC with read-only standby in central DC. Pros: lowest cross-site latency for control-plane operations; Cons: higher ops handoff.
   - Option B: Centralized control plane in their central DC + regional worker pools. Pros: simpler upgrades; Cons: needs stable MPLS and NAT traversal for kubelet.

2) Node pools & sizing (pilot site):
   - inference-hot: 3 x n1-standard-16 + local 2TB NVMe (for KV cache + model shards) — packed for concurrency and fast PS util.
   - batch-sync: 2 x n1-standard-8 + 4TB HDD for buffering before replication.
   - infra-system: 2 x n1-standard-4 (control-plane proxies, logging sidecars, CSI controllers)

3) Storage:
   - PV classes: local-ssd (ephemeral NVMe for model cache, not for durable state), blockstore-encrypted (CSI with KMS integration) for persistent volumes.
   - Provide fallback to NFS on-site appliance if CSI attach fails; strict IO QoS for inference pods.

4) Networking gating checklist:
   - Kube API reachable for control plane ops (whitelist Redwood collector IPs if using managed ops).
   - Outbound HTTPS allowed to object-store endpoints for replication and registry pulls (initial images).
   - UDP traffic for device heartbeats usually remains local; confirm MPLS routing for cross-site Pod to Pod if required.

5) Security: must support KMS integration (they asked about HSM / KMS), node attestation, and RBAC for device-facing services.

Next steps / mutual action plan (pilot timeline):
- Thu Jul 16: network topology call with WarehouseWorks network team (Neha to lead).
- Mon Jul 20: pilot SOW draft + preliminary node sizing (Karthik).
- Fri Jul 24: on-site inventory validation and handbook (Marissa).

Please review and I'll send a consolidated reply back to David & Sophie with the proposed SOW draft and network diagram placeholder.

Irene

- Deliverables: cluster buildbook, CSI/KMS test plan, network gating checklist, and a 4-week operator handoff.
- Security evidence: we'll return the redacted security questionnaire + SOC2 mapping during the SOW review (attached).

Attachments: sow-draft.docx (contains milestones & acceptance criteria), network-diagram.png (placeholder).

Proposed dates: network call Jul 16 (as Irene suggested), SOW review Jul 20, pilot install week Aug 9 (onsite prep Aug 2).

A few open technical questions we need answered before SOW finalization:
- Confirm whether the NVMe is locally attached (and whether it's persistent across reboots) or an ESD-backed appliance.
- Does warehouse firewall allow egress to our container registry (ghcr.io) and the object-store for replication?
- Do you require encrypted PVCs with customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS) or is Redwood KMS acceptable for pilot?

David / Sophie — if these dates look ok, we'll push the SOW for review end of day Mon Jul 20.

Thanks,
